nodes.label: Callbacks must be strictly non-blocking (unmanaged C++ worker thread)
nodes.description: Because callbacks originate from an unmanaged C++ worker thread, they must remain strictly non-blocking: copy data and return 0 quickly.
nodes.norm_label: callbacks must be strictly non-blocking (unmanaged c++ worker thread)
nodes.rationale: Blocking in the callback stalls the DLL's polling worker thread.

nodes.label: §7 Asynchronous Callback Architecture
nodes.description: Callbacks originate from an unmanaged C++ worker thread and must be strictly non-blocking; package-level syscall.NewCallback singletons; RWMutex-protected copy into lastRecord.

nodes.label: onErrorCallback(code, messagePtr uintptr) uintptr
nodes.description: Prints '[DLL ERROR] Event Code: %d' with the code and returns 0.

nodes.label: onDataCallback(ptr uintptr) uintptr
nodes.description: Returns 0 if ptr == 0; otherwise copies the CncMasterSnapshot from unmanaged memory under dataMutex into lastRecord, sets hasRecord, returns 0.

nodes.label: Package-level callback singletons (syscall.NewCallback)
nodes.description: dataCallback = syscall.NewCallback(onDataCallback); errCallback = syscall.NewCallback(onErrorCallback) declared as package-level singletons (stdcall callbacks passed as dataCb/errCb).
nodes.rationale: syscall.NewCallback slots are limited and never freed, so callbacks are created once.

nodes.label: Mutex-protected copy: dataMutex sync.RWMutex -> lastRecord/hasRecord
nodes.description: dataMutex.Lock(); lastRecord = *(*CncMasterSnapshot)(unsafe.Pointer(ptr)); hasRecord = true; dataMutex.Unlock() — copies unmanaged memory buffer into managed Go struct.
nodes.rationale: Copy out of DLL-owned memory under a lock so the renderer reads a consistent snapshot.

nodes.label: stdcall Callbacks via syscall.NewCallback
nodes.rationale: Callbacks run on an unmanaged C++ worker thread so must be non-blocking.

nodes.rationale: Eager load surfaces missing DLL dependencies at startup instead of at first call.
